newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore bourse opens flat, seen steady.
newsitem.headline: Singapore bourse opens flat, seen steady.

text.p: Singapore's benchmark share index looked set on Friday to end its third straight week with no significant movement, dealers said.

By 0230 GMT, the benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index was down just 0.56 points at 2,082.67, almost unchanged from its position at last Friday's close of 2,077.20 points. Two weeks ago it closed at 2,064.52 and three weeks ago at 2,076.65.
"I realised this morning why I felt I hadn't been doing any business," said one institutional broker. "I hadn't."
Total volume for the first one and a half hours was under 27 million shares with losers outnumbering gainers by 92 to 60.

Dealers said part of the reason for the lack of volume was that investors were holding off ahead of a crop of economic data due to be published soon. Singapore's third quarter growth figure is expected to show a rise in the city-state's gross domestic product of only two to three percent year-on-year.

Shares in Singapore Telecom fell back four cents to S$3.24 in early trade after rising sharply on Thursday on hopes it would benefit from inclusion in the new Singapore Regional Index, of which it comprises more than 10 percent.
